“Untouched” leads have no logged contact attempt yet — a diligence signal independent of lead quality. Rows shaded red sit meaningfully below their own team’s median on lead→admission conversion (among BDEs with 10+ leads) — a flag to look into, not an automatic verdict, since lead mix still varies BDE to BDE.
Scale/Optimize/Pause calls are made within each team and dimension by comparing conversion rate and CAC against that team’s own median — a Global campaign is never compared to a Saudi one. Needs at least 20 leads (or meaningful spend) to get a call; smaller campaigns are marked Insufficient data. Degree/Channel filters above narrow these tables; Entity does not (both teams always shown).

Alerts compare the selected date range’s second half vs first half (change the From/To pickers above to widen or narrow the comparison window) — except the lead-flow check, which looks at the whole range at once. These are heuristic flags meant to prompt a look, not automatic verdicts.

Lead-flow breakage

Meta counts a lead every time someone submits an on-platform lead form (“On-Facebook leads”). If meaningfully more of those show up in Meta than land in the CRM for the same campaign, leads are likely getting lost between the ad platform and the CRM — a sync/integration issue, not a marketing one.
Campaign▾ Entity▾ Meta leads▾ CRM leads▾ Gap▾ Gap %▾ Spend (AED)▾

BDE performance drop

Compares each BDE’s own recent conversion/diligence against their own earlier baseline within the selected range — not against peers. Needs at least 10 leads in each half.
BDE▾ Entity▾ Earlier conv. %▾ Recent conv. %▾ Earlier untouched %▾ Recent untouched %▾ Flag▾

Campaign trend degradation

Compares each campaign’s own recent CPL and lead→admission conversion against its own earlier baseline. Only at campaign level today — ad-set/ad-level trend data isn’t pulled from Supermetrics yet.

Methodology & scope

  • Sources. CRM export Reports20260829085255.xlsx (31,322 leads, Jan–Aug 2026) joined to Meta Ads (Supermetrics) across the BIGNxt, BIG Academy KSA and BIUC ad accounts — all three bill in AED. Google Ads and LinkedIn Ads leads already appear in the CRM channel breakdown, but their ad-spend accounts are not yet connected in Supermetrics, so spend/CPL/CAC for those channels is blank until connected — the dashboard will pick them up automatically once authorized.
  • Entity split (Global vs Saudi). A lead is Saudi if its degree is Bachelor’s (offered only at the Riyadh campus, so always routed to the Saudi team), or if its campaign name / country field references Saudi Arabia, Riyadh or Jeddah. Everything else is Global. Country free-text in the CRM is inconsistent (40+ spellings of “Saudi Arabia”), so campaign naming is treated as the primary signal.
  • Degree bucket. Derived from “Level of study” (CRM) or the campaign name (Ads): Bachelors/BBA/BSc → Bachelor; Masters/Executive Masters/MBA/DBA/Doctorate → Masters; certificates/diplomas/unlabeled → Other.
  • Funnel stages. The CRM “Status” field is a current snapshot, not a stage-entry log, so this funnel shows where leads sit today, not cohort conversion over time. Stages roll up as: New Lead → Working (Recontactable/Non Contactable/Call Back/Future follow up) → Qualified (Prospect/Hot Prospect) → Meeting Scheduled → Meeting Done → Application Filled → Admission Done. Not Interested/Not Eligible/Cold are tracked separately as Lost.
  • Campaign join. Ad spend is matched to CRM leads by exact campaign name, which recovers 98% of tracked ad spend (149 of 183 Meta campaigns). Unmatched campaigns are typically traffic/awareness/engagement objectives that aren’t expected to log CRM leads directly.
  • Stage-to-stage conversion. Because Status is a snapshot, “reached a stage” is approximated as leads currently sitting at that stage or any later one — a lead that reached Meeting Done and was later marked Lost is not counted as having reached it, so these rates are a floor, not exact cohort tracking. “Payment” is approximated by the Admission Done status, since the CRM export has no separate payment-received field.
  • Summary & BDE tabs are always entity-split. Global and Saudi run separate budgets/targets, so both tabs show Global and Saudi side by side rather than toggling between them; the top Entity control only scopes Trends and the campaign table. Degree/Channel filters still narrow the Summary tab (not BDE, which isn’t cross-tabbed with those).
  • Geography. Read primarily from the campaign’s own target-country naming (campaigns are named per country, which is more reliable than the CRM’s free-text Country field), falling back to a normalized version of that Country field for organic/offline leads with no country-specific campaign. Saudi cities (Riyadh/Jeddah/Dammam/Medina) roll up into one Saudi Arabia row; a handful of campaigns target a joint region (e.g. “Qatar & UAE”) and are kept as one row rather than split.
  • BDE performance. One row per CRM “Lead owner.” “Untouched %” is the share of a BDE’s leads still sitting in an Untouched/Not-enquired sub-status — a proxy for leads that were never worked, independent of lead quality. Rows are flagged when lead→admission conversion falls below 60% of their own team’s median, restricted to BDEs with at least 10 leads so small books don’t get flagged on noise; it is a starting point for a conversation, not a performance verdict, since lead mix still varies BDE to BDE.
  • Recommendations tab. Campaigns/geography/channels are scored within their own team by comparing conversion rate and CAC against that team’s own median — Scale (better than median on both, real volume already), Optimize (mixed signals, or acceptable conversion but weak CAC or vice versa), Pause (worse than median on both, with real spend already committed), Insufficient data (under 20 leads and little spend — too early to call). This is a heuristic ranking, not a budget-allocation model — use it to prioritize where to look, not as the final word.
  • Alerts tab. Three independent checks: (1) Lead-flow breakage compares Meta’s own on-platform lead count per campaign against what actually landed in the CRM for the whole selected range — a large, consistent gap points at a tracking/sync problem, not a marketing one. (2) BDE performance drop and (3) Campaign trend degradation both split the selected date range in half and compare each BDE’s or campaign’s own second half against its own first half — so make the range wide enough (e.g. 8+ weeks) for both halves to hold a meaningful sample. None of this is available at ad-set/ad level yet since that granularity hasn’t been pulled from Supermetrics.
